blocks.text: A type falls into one of two groups. **Copy types** (numbers, `bool`, `str`, plain structs, arrays of Copy elements) live on the stack and are cheap to copy. **Move types** (`List`, `Box`, `string`, and anything that contains them) own heap memory; they are never copied, only **moved** (so there is no double free).
With numbers, `b = a` copies; `a` stays usable. With lists, `list_b = list_a` moves ownership: only `list_b` is valid now. If you want an independent copy you write `.clone()`.

blocks.prompt: Take a `.clone()` of the list `original` named `dup`, push 99 onto `dup`, and print the length of both lists.

blocks.why: `List` lives on the heap so it is moved; numbers are copied.
